title: feat(data-objectstack): MetadataDraftHeader declares the spec row's member
body:
Fixes #12413
Clause-②: yes (widening)

`MetadataDraftHeader`, the declared row of `MetadataClient.listDrafts()`, now declares the `member` that `@objectstack/spec` declares on `ListDraftsResponseSchema.drafts[]` and the served rows carry. The publish-all hook reads it without a cast, and `publishDraft()`'s advisory event names the member a publish named.

## Public-surface change (for the contract review)

All of it is in `@object-ui/data-objectstack`. Nothing is removed or narrowed.

| Symbol | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `MetadataDraftHeader` | interface with `type: string`, `name: string`, `packageId: string or null`, `updatedAt: string or null`, `updatedBy: string or null` | interface that extends a `Pick` of the spec row `ListDraftsResponse['drafts'][number]` over those same five keys, plus `member?: ListDraftsRow['member']` (resolves to `string or undefined`) |
| `MetadataSaveAdvisoryEvent` | `type`, `name`, `mode`, `door`, `advisories` | the same five, plus optional `member` (typed as `MetadataDraftHeader['member']`) |
| `MetadataClient.publishDraft` | emits the advisory event with `type`, `name`, `door`, `mode` | the same, plus `member` only when `options.member` is a non-empty string (the same rule as the `?member=` query parameter) |

- **Derived, not hand-copied** (the triage direction). The five existing keys come from the spec row by `Pick` and their types are unchanged: the spec row declares exactly `string` / `string or null` for them, pinned key by key with type equality in the new test. `member` is declared in the interface body and typed by the spec row's own `member`. It is declared in the body rather than picked because an interface whose body is empty is refused by `@typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type`.
- **Why the spec row's `label` is not picked.** The spec declares `label` REQUIRED (nullable) on the same row. Picking it would add a required key no caller asked for, and would have this client assert a server vintage it cannot check: the same reason `MetadataPublishPackageDraftsResult` is `Partial`. It is listed under Acceptance notes.
- **Shape kind kept.** `MetadataDraftHeader` stays an `interface`, so declaration merging by a consumer keeps working. The published `dist/index.d.ts` carries the new declaration and imports `ListDraftsResponse` from `@objectstack/spec/api`, which is already a runtime dependency of the package.
- **Semver.** `@object-ui/data-objectstack: minor` (an additive widening of two published types; objectui never declares `major`). `@object-ui/app-shell: patch` (a shipped file changes: a cast is removed, with no behaviour change).

## What changed in app-shell

`usePublishAllDrafts`: `((await client.listDrafts?.({})) as any[]) || []` becomes `(await client.listDrafts?.({})) || []`, and `d.member as string` becomes `d.member` after the existing `typeof` check. The runtime expression is the same, and so are the URLs it sends.

## Premise check (rule 6)

- **The card's premise does not hold for `usePendingDrafts`.** `fetchPendingDrafts` does not read through `MetadataClient.listDrafts()` or `MetadataDraftHeader`. It does its own `fetch` of `_drafts` and types the rows as `Array of Record of string to unknown`. Its `d.member as string` follows a `typeof d.member === 'string'` check on an `unknown` value. It is not an `any` cast, and this widening cannot reach it. The file is left untouched, so the ruling's "no behaviour change" holds trivially there. Its pins (`usePendingDrafts.*.test.tsx`, `DraftChangesPanel.bundleMember-12271.test.tsx`) are green in the runs below.
- A1 holds: the interface lives in `packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts`, and the spec exports `ListDraftsResponse` (`z.input` of `ListDraftsResponseSchema`; the schema has no defaults or transforms, so the `z.infer` face `ListDraftsResponseParsed` is the same row).
- A2 holds: the event type is published, and adding the field is one optional member plus one conditional spread at the single emit in `publishDraft`. The other emits (`publish`, `save`, the batch door) are unchanged.
- A3: the type-level pin is `metadata-client.draftHeaderMember-12413.types.test.ts`, type-checked by the package's own `tsc --noEmit` (its program is `src/**`, tests included).

## Verification (head `236904f8d`)

- Closure build: `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` exit 0, then `@object-ui/data-objectstack` rebuilt on the final head (its `dist/index.d.ts` carries the new interface).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack type-check` exit 0. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exit 0 against the rebuilt dist.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/data-objectstack/ packages/app-shell/src/preview/`: Test Files 116 passed (116), Tests 1319 passed (1319).
- **Reverse check.** The fix was committed first. Deleting the `member` line from the interface (written by `ablation-replace.mjs`, which confirmed anchor count 1 to 0 on disk) turned the data-objectstack type-check red: TS2339 on the pin file's cast-free reads (including the runtime read of `row.member` off each `listDrafts()` row), TS2344 on the key-set equality, and TS2339 on the event's `MetadataDraftHeader['member']`. The file was then restored, and its blob matched HEAD. The first form (dropping `'member'` from the `Pick`) went red the same way before the lint-driven reshape.
- `eslint --no-inline-config`, narrowed to the 3 changed source files: 0 errors, 10 warnings (`no-explicit-any` on lines this diff does not add). Population: the root `eslint.config.js`. File count: 3, from the `--format json` output. Invariance: the config sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- Pre-tsc battery, each exit 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:doc-example-readers`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:icon-record-names`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`. Also exit 0: `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`.
- `check:spec-floors` exits 1 (`no-artifact` on packages this branch did not build). This is the known failure on `main`, tracked as objectui#12334, and it is not touched here.

## Acceptance notes

- `MetadataDraftHeader` still omits the spec row's `label`, and `loadPackageSurfaces` in `packageSurfaces.ts` shows a draft-only item with its machine name as the label. The spec says `label` exists so that such an item is not shown by machine name alone. This is a read-only inference: I did not reproduce it in a running app. Not filed. Carrier: none.
- The batch door's per-element advisory events (`publishPackageDrafts`) carry no `member`. The spec's `published[]` element declares none, so there is nothing to carry. Recorded, not filed.
